name: Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.

corporate_actions.event: Closed AssuredPartners acquisition (~$13.8bn); funded by $8.5bn Dec-2024 equity offering + $1.3bn overallotment + $5.0bn senior notes

geography.fx_notes: PitchBook/Morningstar: about a third of revenue international (Australia, Canada, NZ, UK) -> US roughly two-thirds (INFERENCE); AssuredPartners (US) raises US share. 10-K split not extracted.

kpis.name: Brokerage organic (base commissions & fees / supplemental / contingent)
Acquisitions closed
kpis.value: 33 in 2025 with >$3.5bn annualised revenue; 19 YTD 2026 incl. 5 in Q3 (~$102m revenue)

kpis.name: Brokerage interest income, premium finance and other
kpis.value: $732m (2025) vs $420m (2024) - includes interest on AP pre-funding cash

acquisitions.earnouts: not disclosed in sources used (10-K note not extracted)
acquisitions.notes: AssuredPartners ~$13.8bn (closed 18-Aug-2025) + 32 other deals; >$3.5bn acquired revenue. AP multiple not disclosed in sources used.
19 tuck-ins YTD; AP synergies $160m annualised by YE26, $325m by early 2028; AP may dilute brokerage organic 40-50bp in early 2027

management.ceo: J. Patrick Gallagher, Jr. (Chairman, President & CEO)
management.succession_notes: Founding-family CEO; long tenure = key-person risk; no public succession timetable found
management.guidance_record: Gives detailed quarterly organic outlooks at investor days; Q4-25 brokerage organic 5% 'in line with December commentary' (S6)

ownership.controlling_holders: None (Gallagher family holds small stake; widely held)

evidence: Commission/fee revenue renews annually; RM (claims TPA) contractual (S1)
Organic 9% -> 7% -> 6% -> 5% shows durability but rate sensitivity (S5,S6,S2)
26 consecutive quarters of double-digit adj EBITDAC growth (S3)
B.rationale: Middle-market density and niche practices give pricing power with carriers.

C.rationale: Scale yields rising margins and carrier contingent/supplemental income.

D.rationale: Large fragmented US/intl broker market keeps a long tuck-in runway.

evidence: ~1/3 of revenue international (Aus, Can, NZ, UK) (S1)
Q4-25 organic in line with December guide (S6)
F.rationale: Reliable guidance; succession is the main risk.

evidence: AP funded mostly with equity, keeping leverage ~3.2x (S2,S1)
Serial tuck-ins with stated synergy targets (S4)
G.rationale: Disciplined, equity-heavy funding of large deal; returns on AP still to be proven.

evidence: Middle-market commercial and benefits broking; RM claims administration (S1)
I1.rationale: Middle-market advice relationship-driven; small-commercial and claims TPA more automatable (INFERENCE).

evidence: Large back-office and claims-handling headcount (~72k employees) (S1)
Commission-based pricing; RM fee contracts may pass savings (INFERENCE)
Heavy use of adjusted/'levelized FX' measures; clean energy investments and $713m tax credit carryforwards (S2)

sector_specific.organic_ex_rate_note: INFERENCE: brokerage organic fell from 8.9% (2023) to ~5% (2026) as renewal premium increases moderated; management attributes 2026 to new business and retention with rate tailwind fading. Renewal premium change not extracted in this pass.
sector_specific.contingent_consideration: not disclosed in sources used (earn-out liability in 10-K not extracted)

gates.notes: G1: ~3.2x PitchBook gross debt/EBITDA (post-AP) < 4.0x. G4 not computed here. No pending takeover.

bull_points: Proven tuck-in machine in a fragmented market; AP adds US middle-market density with $325m synergy target.
Most resilient organic among large US retail brokers in the 2026 soft market (5% vs BRO 1.2%).
bear_points: AP integration could dilute organic (40-50bp in early 2027 per management) and margins.
Organic growth has decelerated four years running as rate tailwinds fade.
Key-person and succession risk around long-serving CEO.
thesis_breakers: Brokerage organic < 4% for a full year.
AP synergies below $160m run-rate by end-2026.
